entity_title: Work permit is tied to one employer
fact_text: A third-country national's Romanian work authorisation is tied to one specific employer: IGI guidance states you may be employed by only a single employer, person or entity. Working for a different employer requires that new employer to obtain a fresh work permit.
evidence_quote: You can be employed in Romania by a single employer, person or entity.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a Romanian work permit lets you take any job. Actually it authorises work for one named employer only. Action: any change of employer requires the new employer to obtain a new work permit before you start.

entity_title: Only the employer can obtain the work permit
fact_text: The relocating worker cannot apply for their own Romanian work permit. Per EURAXESS Romania (government portal), a work permit can only be obtained by the employer, who submits the documents and pays the fees at the General Inspectorate for Immigration (IGI).
evidence_quote: A work permit can only be obtained by the employer, natural person or legal entity

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the relocating employee starts the immigration process. Actually the Romanian employer must initiate and obtain the work permit first. Action: nothing can begin until a Romanian employer files on your behalf.

entity_title: Work permits are capped by an annual quota
fact_text: Issuing a Romanian work permit to a third-country national is conditioned on falling within the annual quota of newly-admitted foreign workers, set each year by Government Decision. Once the quota is exhausted, no further permits are granted that year.
evidence_quote: You fall within the annual quota approved by Government Decision

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a valid job offer guarantees a work permit. Actually permits are granted only within a capped annual quota set by Government Decision. Action: apply early in the year; if the quota is used up, hiring waits for the next allocation.

entity_title: Vacancy must be un-fillable by local/EU workers
fact_text: Before a third-country national can be hired, the employer must show the vacant post cannot be filled by Romanian, EU/EEA citizens or permanent residents in Romania. This labour-market test is a precondition for the work permit.
evidence_quote: The vacant positions cannot be filled by Romanian citizens of EU Member States / EEA or by permanent residents in Romania

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any role can be given to a chosen foreign candidate. Actually the employer must first show the post cannot be filled by Romanian/EU/EEA or permanent-resident workers. Action: document the failed local recruitment before applying.

entity_title: Work permit fee (permanent worker) is EUR 100
fact_text: For a permanent worker (and several other categories), the employer pays a fee equivalent in RON to EUR 100 when submitting the work permit application to IGI. It is an employer cost, separate from the visa fee the worker pays abroad.
evidence_quote: the employer will pay a tax in RON equivalent to 100 EUR

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed immigration fees fall on the relocating employee. Actually the work permit fee (EUR 100 equivalent for permanent workers) is paid by the employer at application. Action: budget it as an employer cost, distinct from the EUR 120 visa fee.

entity_title: Work permit cancelled when the job ends
fact_text: IGI cancels the work/posting permit upon termination of the individual employment contract. Because the permit underpins the employment residence right, ending or losing the job removes the basis for the foreign national's authorised stay.
evidence_quote: upon termination of the individual employment contract or secondment.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a work/residence permit stays valid until its printed expiry. Actually it is cancelled when the employment contract ends. Action: on resignation or dismissal, secure a new employer's permit or change of status quickly to stay lawful.

entity_title: Blue Card: free job mobility only after 12 months
fact_text: An EU Blue Card holder in Romania may work for individuals or legal persons without a separate work permit only after 12 months of legal employment as a highly qualified worker. In the first 12 months the job stays permit- and employer-bound.
evidence_quote: foreigners possessing a valid EU Blue Card, after 12 months of legal employment in Romania, as a highly qualified worker

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the EU Blue Card gives immediate freedom to change jobs. Actually free labour-market access in Romania comes only after 12 months of legal highly-qualified employment. Action: do not change employer in the first year without checking permit rules.

entity_title: Long-stay employment visa fee is EUR 120
fact_text: After the employer obtains the work permit, the worker applies abroad for the Romanian long-stay visa for employment (D/AM). The visa fee is EUR 120, paid in the state where the application is made, before travelling to Romania.
evidence_quote: The visa fee is 120 EUR and is paid in the State where you make the request.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the visa is obtained after arriving in Romania. Actually the long-stay employment visa (EUR 120) must be obtained abroad at a Romanian consulate before travel. Action: apply at the consulate in your country of residence, not in Romania.

fact_text: The Romanian long-stay employment visa is granted for only 90 days. Within that window the worker must apply to IGI for the single permit (residence permit), which must be filed in person at least 30 days before the stay granted by the visa expires.
evidence_quote: The long stay visa is granted for a period of 90 days, with one or more trips.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the long-stay visa covers the whole assignment. Actually it authorises only 90 days, within which you must obtain the residence/single permit. Action: book the IGI single-permit appointment right after arrival, well before day 60.

entity_title: Proof of legal housing required for the permit
fact_text: To obtain the single permit (residence permit for work), a third-country national must submit proof of legal ownership or possession of the living space, in original and duplicate. A temporary or informal address is not accepted.
evidence_quote: proof of legal ownership of the living space in original and duplicate

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed housing can be arranged after getting the permit. Actually documented legal proof of the living space is a required document to obtain the single permit. Action: secure a registered lease or property proof before the IGI appointment.

fact_text: A non-resident individual present in Romania for more than 183 days in any 12 consecutive months must submit ANAF's fiscal-residence questionnaire (form Z015) to the competent fiscal body within 30 days of meeting the 183-day threshold.
evidence_quote: The non-resident individuals have to submit the questionnaire to the competent central fiscal body, within 30 days from the fulfilment of the deadline of 183 days of presence in Romania.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed tax residency is handled only via the annual return. Actually ANAF requires a dedicated arrival questionnaire (Z015) filed within 30 days of crossing 183 days. Action: diarise the 183-day date and file the questionnaire on time.

entity_title: Romanian tax residents taxed on worldwide income
fact_text: Once a foreign individual is established as a Romanian tax resident, they have a full fiscal obligation and are taxed on income from any source, both from Romania and from outside Romania, from the date they become resident.
evidence_quote: being subject to income tax for the income obtained from any source, both from Romania and from outside Romania

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed only Romanian-source salary is taxed in Romania. Actually, once you become a Romanian tax resident you are taxed on worldwide income. Action: review foreign income, treaty relief and reporting around the residency date.
